- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimates prices in the latter half of the forecast, particularly when true values show strong upward momentum.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in upward trends.
- Overreacts to short-term volatility, overshooting peaks and failing to capture sustained momentum.
- Fails to account for mean reversion in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, leading to persistent overestimation.
- When true prices rise sharply, model forecasts remain flat or slightly below, then catch up too late.
- Model exhibits bias toward higher values in the first 10 days of the forecast, especially when historical mean is rising.
- Underestimates downward corrections after spikes, often missing the full extent of price drop.
